questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical RBAC auditing skills within the CKAD scope, including multi-namespace governance, secure logging, and egress constraints.

## Key Concepts

- **RBAC objects**: RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings, and ServiceAccounts at the namespace level
- **ConfigMap-driven policy**: External policy reference for audit rules
- **Namespace-scoped auditing**: Decentralized audit model vs. cluster-wide approaches
- **Pod lifecycle**: InitContainers for tool installation, readiness/liveness probes for reliability
- **Storage**: PVC-backed logging at /logs
- **Network security**: Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress to the audit endpoint

## Trade-offs

- **Pros**: Decentralized scaling, namespace isolation, ConfigMap flexibility for policy updates
- **Cons**: Resource overhead per namespace, potential for policy drift, Secret management complexity, duplicated effort across namespaces

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rbac-policy
data:
  policy.yaml: |-
    allowedBindings:
      - kind: User
        name: admin
    maxServiceAccounts: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-token: <token>
  endpoint: https://audit.example.com/api/v1/digest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rbac-auditor
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rbac-auditor
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - "wget -qO /tools/curl https://curl.se/download && wget -qO /tools/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /tools/*"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                kubectl get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings,serviceaccounts -o json > /logs/snapshot.json
                curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @/logs/snapshot.json $ENDPOINT
                sleep 3600
              done
          env:
            - name: TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: bearer-token
            - name: ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: endpoint
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-logs
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to orchestrate time-based batch workloads, integrate ConfigMaps and Secrets with PVs, and enforce idempotence and rollback for Kubernetes workload automation.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob with Job template and parallelism
- ConfigMap mounted as /etc/reconcile
- PVC mounted at /data/reconcile
- Secret-provided DB credentials via env vars
- Resource requests/limits and graceful termination
- checksum/config annotation to trigger updates
- RBAC: RoleBinding for service account

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron
  namespace: data-warehouse
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            checksum/config: "abcdef1234" # placeholder hash
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: reconcile-sa
          containers:
          - name: reconciler
            image: my-registry/reconcile:latest
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
            volumeMounts:
            - name: reconcile-rules
              mountPath: /etc/reconcile
            - name: reconcile-output
              mountPath: /data/reconcile
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "200m"
                memory: "256Mi"
              limits:
                cpu: "500m"
                memory: "512Mi"
          volumes:
          - name: reconcile-rules
            configMap:
              name: reconcile-rules
          - name: reconcile-output
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: reconcile-pvc
          terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

```yaml

apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: data-warehouse
  name: reconcile-cron-role
rules:
- apiGroups: ["batch"]
  resources: ["jobs"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron-binding
  namespace: data-warehouse
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: reconcile-sa
  namespace: data-warehouse
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: reconcile-cron-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to translate dynamic allowlists into enforced Kubernetes NetworkPolicy rules while maintaining per-namespace isolation. It combines ConfigMap-driven configuration, DNS resolution, RBAC scoping, and observability—all core CKAD competencies.

## Key Concepts

- **NetworkPolicy**: Enforces egress rules at the pod level using `ipBlock` selectors. Note that egress rules require CNI support for enforcement.

- Forgetting DNS egress rules causes complete name resolution failure

- Resolving hostnames to IPs at apply time introduces a lag between DNS changes and policy updates
- Not all CNIs fully support egress policies; test enforcement in your target environment

- Consider using a mutating webhook or operator for more robust reconciliation
- Implement metric export (Prometheus) for monitoring resolution success rates
- Add retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network failures

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```
